tldr: TL;DR: Chile is the one South American market on our export list and the longest sea leg we quote. We ship BWR, IS 710 BWP marine, commercial, film-faced shuttering and packing-grade plywood from Cochin Port, quoted in USD, FOB Cochin by default. Specify the bond for the voyage: MR is moisture-resistant, not waterproof. We do not publish a transit time for this lane because your forwarder chooses the routing. Quote replies within one business day.
ports_ship: the Chilean discharge port you nominate
faq: How long does a container take from Kochi to Chile?

We do not publish a transit time for this lane. The service and any transhipment your forwarder books is what decides it, and on the longest lane we run a made-up number would be the most expensive thing on the page. What we do put in writing is the schedule at our end: production lead time, the inspection window before loading, stuffing at the factory 40 km from Cochin Port, and gate-in.
Which bond grade should I order for a voyage this long?

MR is moisture-resistant, not waterproof, and it is the wrong board to put through weeks of sea air and then store in a damp yard. Where the panel will sit in humid conditions after it lands, specify BWR; where it will actually be wet, IS 710 BWP marine. We confirm the bond on the proforma invoice and every grade ships with its technical data sheet.
Do you quote CIF Chile, or only FOB Cochin?

FOB Cochin is the default, in USD under Incoterms 2020. FCA Cochin, CFR or CIF are quoted where agreed, against the freight the routing you choose actually attracts. Standard products ship on 50% advance with the balance before dispatch; custom specifications are 100% advance, by bank transfer (T/T).
How are the panels packed for the voyage?

Palletised and strapped for sea transit. Plywood is dense and weighs out before it cubes out, so we load to the lower of the ship-line payload, about 26.7 tonnes, and the road limit at your end, and confirm the sheet count with the net and gross weights on the proforma invoice.
